answer: Non-transferable reputation stops sybil farming at the root: standing is earned only by completing verified work and is bound to one identity, like a pearl that grows inside a shell and cannot be transplanted. New identities start at zero trust, face a cooling-off period and rate limits before they can transact, while an atlas of past behaviour lets peers spot new accounts. Standing decays with inactivity, so an attacker spawning a hundred fresh agents must pay the time cost for each, and a sonnet of praise from a fake peer counts for nothing because only earned identities can endorse.
